correctness.rationale: The 16-bit feedback masks parameterize exactly the successor permutations of binary order-five de Bruijn cycles via paired conjugate five-bit states, with no rotational overcount because every Hamiltonian cycle can be rooted at state 0. One valid cross-join changes exactly two distinct feedback bits, splitting and then rejoining the 32-cycle; valid neighboring masks are recognized by an exhaustive criterion. An independently written verifier exhaustively tested all 65,536 feedback masks (2048 valid), formed all 120 double-bit changes per valid mask and BFS from each of 2048 vertices in the resulting undirected graph. It independently obtained 38,704 edges, distance counts (38,704,305,376,758,800,710,976,254,800,27,104,368) at distances 1..7, eccentricities 48,1264,736 for values 5,6,7, diameter 7 and radius 5. The proof is finite and exhaustive, not sampled; the earlier degree table is treated only as a prior checksum.

value.rationale: Cross-join connectivity of de Bruijn cycles is known, but the number of *validity-preserving single cross-join operations* needed between two cycles is a directly motivated natural graph metric. The 2048-vertex order-five graph has a complete quantitative metric census and exact seven-step worst case, 48 central cycles, and distribution of all unordered pair distances. This is a substantial complete finite graph classification, not an unmotivated fragment of a larger census.
